findings.where: Screen 2 (Between shunt and series), the words around the picture
findings.what: This SHOW screen carries about 173 words: the task, a 64-word assumption paragraph and a 35-word say line make 108 words of prose, and the worked panel adds 65 more. Cut the paragraph to the two rules (torque goes with flux x Ia, speed goes with back-emf / flux) and move the example values into the worked panel.

findings.where: Screen 2, the plot's red band at 1.25 and the red no-load readout
findings.what: The 'example limit' never says what it limits. It also turns a standard compound motor's normal no-load speed red: screen 4's cited 30% regulation gives 1.30, which contradicts 'safe to run light'. Either drop the band and keep red for 'speed rises with load', 'over 2.00' and 'runs away', or say plainly what it stands for and put it above the cited figures.

findings.where: Screen 2, the worked panel's heading and its 'Running light' line
findings.what: Nothing on screen says that 1 - 0.05 x Ia is the back-emf (the supply less the 5% armature-circuit drop) or that dividing by 0.95 makes rated speed 1.00, so the key step is skipped. 'The top is (1 - 0.0025) / 0.95 = ... = 1.05' also misnames things: the top is 0.9975, and 1.05 is the top divided by 0.95.

findings.where: Screen 2 task 'Then switch to Differential' (and screen 1)
findings.what: He is asked to switch to Differential before any screen has said what differential compound is. The brief promised screen 1 would say it: reverse the series field and the fields oppose; that is differential compound, rarely used because it can be unstable. Add that line to screen 1 and keep it under 90 words, for example by shortening the long/short shunt line.

'A regenerative drive needs a straight shunt motor. Otherwise the series field opposes the shunt field when it regenerates.' uses jargon no lesson has explained. It also skips the step that makes it true: when the motor brakes, the armature current reverses, and that current runs through the series field. Say this plainly in two short sentences or cut it.

findings.where: Screen 7, the reason shown after answering
findings.what: 'check the interpole polarity and the brush position next' brings in interpoles, which lessons 6 to 8 never teach. Either explain them in one short sentence or keep only 'then check the brush position'.

findings.where: Book text: explain.text and practice.text in i8.lesson.verified.json
findings.what: The chapter has eleven footnotes, against a rule of a few. Five are in explain.text on plain claims he would never look up on a job, such as 'It may even rise slightly.[^12]', 'It can become unstable.[^13]' and the closing bold sentence [^14]. Keep footnotes only on the 15 to 25% and 30% regulation figures and perhaps the polarity rule.

findings.where: Screen 2, the line 'Flux = shunt part + series part x Ia'
findings.what: This is only the Cumulative rule. On Differential the worked panel subtracts, so say 'plus the series part, or minus it on Differential'.

findings.where: Screen 2, Series share slider on Differential
findings.what: On Differential the share jumps back to 50% and nothing on screen says why. Add one short sentence: 'On Differential the share stops at 50%.'

findings.where: Screen 2, 'The 2.00 current is the top of the usual starting limit. That limit is 125 to 200% of full load.'
findings.what: This reads twice. For example: 'The plot runs to twice rated current. A starter usually holds the starting current to 125 to 200% of full load.'

findings.where: Screen 3, hint for 'It hardly changes, like a shunt motor'
findings.what: 'Less flux needs more speed' is terse. Better: 'With less flux, it must turn faster to make the same back-emf.'
Add 'at the same current', as the Keep this card does. A starter sets the starting current, so the comparison only holds like for like.

findings.where: Screen 5, Limits row, 'The no-load speed gets very high.'
findings.what: This is firmer than the source ('may result') and the Keep this card ('can get very high'). Use 'can get very high'.
'Safety first: Isolate, lock off and prove dead first.' says 'first' twice. Dropping the second one also brings the screen from 93 words to under 90.

findings.where: Screen 7, hint for 'The brushes have worn down'
findings.what: 'They make a motor weak' is unsourced. Keep only what is needed: 'Worn brushes spark and make poor contact. They do not make the speed rise with load.'

findings.where: Screens 3 and 7, the choice buttons (film s2)
findings.what: A one-line choice ('It runs away, like a series motor') is centred, while the two-line choices are left-aligned. Align them all left.

The brief promised a comparison of all three DC motors that includes where each is used. Add a row: series for hoists and traction, shunt for steady speed, compound for presses and shears. Also, 'Speed goes with E / flux' never says E is the back-emf. Write 'back-emf E'.

The screen never says what the two fields buy you. Before the picture, one line would carry the why: 'a harder start than a shunt motor, yet a definite speed running light'. Fit it within the 90-word budget together with the differential line.
